title.narrative: Regional and sub-regional constituents have strengthened institutional capacities for improved productivity growth in Africa including inclusive transformation for decent work in the informal economy

description.narrative:
The informal economy in Africa is large and growing rapidly. Self-employment, a vulnerable form of employment, dominates, especially in labor-intensive service sectors, leading to weak economic outcomes such as lower per capita incomes, greater poverty, less financial development, and weaker investment and productivity. Efforts to formalize these economies are recognized as requiring an inclusive approach and long-term investment.
The Programme and Budget 2024-2025 will focus on three key areas: addressing challenges and opportunities for productivity enhancement, enterprise development, decent job creation, and entrepreneurship development; supporting Member States in designing and implementing integrated approaches to enterprise formalization, including simplifying and digitalizing business registration processes, creating effective incentives, and strengthening partnerships; and operationalizing findings from ongoing or planned research on international labor standards, protection at work, social protection, and policy coherence.
The proposal builds on recent measures, including a 2023 policy conference with the African Union and a mapping of actions taken by various member states. The program will target selected countries based on the prevalence of informality, decent work deficits, existing collaborations, and government commitment to formalization. Key partners include the African Union, UNDP, and UNESCO.
